beats.on_screen_text: This scale is level. What's in each bag?
beats.visual: A two-pan scale, perfectly level. Left pan: 3 closed bags and 5 loose blocks. Right pan: 20 loose blocks. The bags wobble slightly.
beats.voiceover: This scale is level. What's in each bag?

beats.on_screen_text: Every bag holds the same number of blocks. Call it x.
beats.visual: Each bag gets an x label. The equation types itself under the scale, each term under the thing it stands for.
beats.voiceover: Every bag holds the same number of blocks. Call it x.

beats.on_screen_text: Take the 5 loose blocks off the left...
beats.visual: 5 blocks lift off the left pan only. The scale tips hard to the right. The +5 in the equation turns muted red.
beats.voiceover: Take the 5 loose blocks off the left...

beats.on_screen_text: ...and it tips. Take 5 off BOTH sides.
beats.visual: Rewind. This time 5 blocks lift off each pan together. The scale stays level. Both sides of the equation show - 5 in highlight.
beats.voiceover: ...and it tips. Take five off both sides.

beats.visual: Left pan: 3 bags. Right pan: 15 blocks. The equation simplifies to 3x = 15.
beats.voiceover: Still level. Three bags weigh the same as fifteen blocks.

beats.on_screen_text: So how many blocks are in ONE bag?
beats.visual: The 15 blocks shuffle but don't split. One bag glows. Freeze.
beats.voiceover: So how many blocks are in one bag?

steps.says: Split both sides into 3 equal groups (divide by 3).

tutor_notes.key_idea: Whatever you do to one side of an equation, you do to the other, so it stays balanced.
tutor_notes.follow_up_prompt: Why did the scale tip when the blocks came off only one side? What does that mean for the equation?

author_notes: The reel stops at 3x = 15 on purpose so the student finishes the last step; the tutor's follow-up should ask for it.
